organism_context: Bacteria (E. coli GuaC), humans (GMPR1/2), trypanosomatids (Leishmania GMPR)
rationale: A single NADPH-dependent deaminating reductase activity (GMP -> IMP + NH3); the CBS/Bateman domain carried by some GMP reductases binds adenylate/guanylate nucleotides and is regulatory, not a second catalytic activity.
direction_note: GMP reductase is physiologically unidirectional in the deaminating direction (GMP + NADPH -> IMP + NH3 + NADP+); ModelSEED writes the aminating direction as forward, which the enzyme does not run, so the LLM council's '<' matches the enzymology.

organism_context: Pseudomonas sp. grown on acetylenic acids (Yamada & Jakoby, 1959); no gene or sequence has ever been assigned
rationale: The only characterisation of EC 4.2.1.27 is a 1959 partial purification from a Pseudomonas sp. that hydrated several alkynoic acids (including 3-butynoate -> acetoacetate); with no sequence, structure or modern re-isolation there is no usable evidence on mono- vs bifunctionality.
direction_note: The reported activity is hydration of the alkyne (3-butynoate + H2O -> acetoacetate); ModelSEED's forward direction is the dehydration, i.e. the reverse of the only experimentally observed reaction.

organism_context: Pseudomonas sp. (Yamada & Jakoby, 1959); same legacy activity as rxn00996, no gene assigned
rationale: Propynoate + H2O -> malonate semialdehyde (3-oxopropanoate) is the type reaction of EC 4.2.1.27, known only from a 1959 partially purified Pseudomonas preparation; no sequence exists, so domain architecture cannot be judged either way.
direction_note: Experimentally the enzyme is a hydratase (propynoate -> 3-oxopropanoate); ModelSEED's forward direction is the dehydration, the reverse of the observed chemistry.

rationale: KEGG R01734 (dimethylbenzimidazole <=> riboflavin) carries no EC and no KO and is flagged by KEGG itself as both 'unclear reaction' and 'incomplete reaction'; ModelSEED's attached name (nicotinate-nucleotide:dimethylbenzimidazole phospho-D-ribosyltransferase, CobT) does not correspond to this equation, and the nearest real chemistry (FMNH2 -> 5,6-dimethylbenzimidazole, BluB) is also not what is written.
direction_note: No enzyme runs this equation in either direction, so neither the ModelSEED nor the LLM call is biologically grounded.

rationale: KEGG R01913 (pyridoxine <=> 1-deoxy-D-xylulose + 4-hydroxy-L-threonine) has no EC, no KO and is explicitly annotated 'incomplete reaction'; the real B6 step (PdxJ, pyridoxine 5'-phosphate synthase) uses the phosphorylated substrates DXP and 4-phosphohydroxy-L-threonine and makes PNP, so it does not catalyse this reaction.

organism_context: Historically reported as a mammalian liver activity; MetaCyc places it in taurine biosynthesis I (PWY-5331). No gene or purified protein.
rationale: KEGG R02434 gives no EC and no KO, only the free-text comment 'cysteinesulfinic acid dehydrogenase'; searches of the sulfonate/taurine literature turned up characterised cysteate synthases, racemases and sulfo-lyases but no identified protein for this NAD-linked cysteate/cysteine-sulfinate interconversion, so functionality cannot be judged.
direction_note: The pathway role is oxidative (cysteine sulfinate -> cysteate) en route to taurine/sulfonates; ModelSEED writes the NADH-driven reductive direction as forward, the reverse of the pathway flux.

enzyme_name: prostaglandin F synthase (PGFS), an aldo-keto reductase
organism_context: Bovine lung PGFS (the enzyme purified and crystallised); human orthologue AKR1C3; a distinct PGFS also exists in Trypanosoma brucei
rationale: A single AKR polypeptide carries two genuinely different catalytic activities at two different active sites: endoperoxide reduction of PGH2 to PGF2alpha and 11-keto reduction of PGD2 to 9alpha,11beta-PGF2.
direction_note: This reaction is the 11-ketoreductase activity written backwards: the enzyme reduces PGD2 to 11-epi-PGF2alpha with NADPH, so the physiological direction is PGD2 -> 11-epi-PGF2alpha, and ModelSEED's equation has additionally dropped the NADPH/NADP+ pair.

organism_context: Bacteria and plants (Arabidopsis THIC); thiamine pyrimidine biosynthesis
rationale: KEGG R03472 maps to EC 4.1.99.17 / KO K03147 (ThiC), a radical-SAM enzyme that converts AIR to HMP-P in one (mechanistically very complex) radical cascade at a single active site - one catalytic activity, not two.
direction_note: ThiC's radical cascade is irreversible in the AIR -> HMP-P direction and consumes SAM; ModelSEED has collapsed the reaction to 'toxopyrimidine => AIR', i.e. the reverse with all cofactors stripped, so the written forward direction is not a real reaction.

rationale: KEGG R03551 carries no EC, no KO and no pathway; the equation (free methanol condensing with gallate, releasing water) matches no characterised enzyme - real gallate/3-O-methylgallate interconversion runs through tetrahydrofolate-dependent O-demethylases (e.g. LigM) or corrinoid methyltransferases in one direction and SAM-dependent O-methyltransferases in the other, none of which fit this cofactor-free equation.

organism_context: Pseudomonas sp. (Yamada & Jakoby, 1958); never sequenced
rationale: The only report is a 1958 partially purified Pseudomonas enzyme converting acetylenedicarboxylate to pyruvate via the enol of oxaloacetate (2-hydroxyethylenedicarboxylate); whether the hydration and the decarboxylation are one concerted active site or two activities on one chain was never resolved and no sequence exists.
direction_note: The observed chemistry is hydration of the alkyne (acetylenedicarboxylate + H2O -> enol-oxaloacetate -> pyruvate + CO2); ModelSEED writes the dehydration as forward, the reverse of the reported reaction.

enzyme_name: no single enzyme (lumped sterol C-4 demethylation)
organism_context: Yeast/fungi (ERG25/26/27), mammals (MSMO1/NSDHL/HSD17B7), plants (SMO1/3betaHSD-D/SR)
rationale: The three ECs attached to this garbled lumped reaction belong to three separate polypeptides of the membrane-bound sterol C-4 demethylation complex (methylsterol monooxygenase, 3beta-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase/C4-decarboxylase, 3-ketosteroid reductase) - a multi-protein complex, not a fused multifunctional chain - and no single enzyme catalyses the reaction as written (2 CO2 + zymosterol => 6 NADPH + 6 O2 + 6 H+ is not balanced chemistry).
direction_note: The underlying biology (sterol demethylation) is O2- and NADPH-consuming and irreversible; the ModelSEED equation has it producing O2 and NADPH, so neither direction call is meaningful for this pseudo-reaction.

organism_context: Pseudomonas putida and other naphthalene degraders; a kappa-class glutathione transferase fold
rationale: A single GSH-dependent cis/trans isomerase activity interconverting HCCA and trans-o-hydroxybenzylidenepyruvate; GSH is a tightly bound cofactor rather than a second (conjugating) catalytic activity, and the GST fold is structural homology, not a second function.
direction_note: Keq is only ~1.5, so the reaction is near-equilibrium, but catabolic flux in naphthalene degradation runs HCCA -> tHBPA; ModelSEED writes tHBPA -> HCCA as forward, i.e. against the pathway direction.

gene_symbols: acetylene hydratase gene of Pelobacter acetylenicus
organism_context: Pelobacter acetylenicus (anaerobic acetylene fermenter); tungsten/iron-sulfur enzyme of the DMSO-reductase family
rationale: A single, unusual non-redox hydration activity (acetylene + H2O -> acetaldehyde) carried out by one W-[4Fe-4S] polypeptide; no second catalytic activity is reported.
direction_note: The enzyme only ever runs the hydration of acetylene to acetaldehyde; ModelSEED's forward direction is the dehydration of acetaldehyde to acetylene, which is both thermodynamically and enzymologically the wrong way round.

organism_context: Chlorocatechol-degrading proteobacteria (Pseudomonas, Ralstonia/Cupriavidus) and Rhodococcus opacus 1CP
rationale: An enolase-superfamily cycloisomerase (EC 5.5.1.7) with one catalytic activity; the chloride elimination that accompanies lactonisation of chloromuconates is part of the same cycloisomerisation mechanism, not a separate dehalogenase domain.
direction_note: Physiologically the enzyme cycloisomerises 2,5-dichloro-cis,cis-muconate to trans-2-chlorodienelactone with chloride release; ModelSEED writes chloride addition (the reverse) as forward.

enzyme_name: L-arginine:inosamine-phosphate amidinotransferase (StrB1; paralogue StrB2 acts on N-amidino-scyllo-inosamine 4-phosphate)
organism_context: Streptomyces griseus, streptomycin biosynthesis
rationale: StrB1/StrB2 are single-activity amidinotransferases of the arginine:glycine amidinotransferase fold, crystallised from S. griseus; only one catalytic activity (amidino group transfer) is described.
direction_note: The biosynthetic direction is amidino transfer from L-arginine onto the inosamine phosphate, releasing L-ornithine; ModelSEED writes ornithine as a substrate and arginine as a product, i.e. the reverse of the biosynthetic step.

enzyme_name: isonitrile hydratase (InhA; a second, unrelated enzyme InhB exists)
organism_context: Pseudomonas putida N19-2 (InhA, DJ-1/ThiJ superfamily) and Arthrobacter pascens F164 (InhB, a 12-subunit homo-oligomer unrelated in sequence)
rationale: Both characterised isonitrile hydratases carry only the hydration activity (cyclohexyl isocyanide + H2O -> N-cyclohexylformamide); the downstream deformylation is a separate protein (NfdA), and InhB's oligomeric state is a homo-oligomer of identical subunits, not a fusion of two activities.
direction_note: The enzyme runs hydration of the isocyanide to the formamide; ModelSEED's forward direction is the dehydration of N-cyclohexylformamide to cyclohexyl isocyanide, the reverse of the catabolic step.

enzyme_name: DoxA, cytochrome P450 monooxygenase (13-deoxydaunorubicin hydroxylase, EC 1.14.13.181)
organism_context: Streptomyces peucetius / Streptomyces sp. C5, daunorubicin-doxorubicin biosynthesis
rationale: KEGG R06689 maps to KO K15955 (DoxA); DoxA is a single-chain P450 that performs three consecutive oxidations on the anthracycline scaffold, but these are iterations of one monooxygenase activity, not distinct catalytic functions, and it needs a separate ferredoxin/reductase partner rather than carrying one.
direction_note: The real reaction is an O2/NADPH-dependent oxidation of 13-dihydrodaunorubicin to daunorubicin and is irreversible in the direction ModelSEED writes as forward; ModelSEED has dropped O2 and NADPH, making it look like a reversible dehydrogenation, which is probably what drew the LLM to '<'.

organism_context: EC 2.4.1.29 is a legacy GDP-glucose-dependent beta-1,4-glucan synthase activity from mung bean; KEGG assigns no KO to R02890. Characterised cellulose synthases are plant CesA and bacterial BcsA (UDP-glucose, EC 2.4.1.12).
rationale: No gene product has ever been cleanly assigned to the GDP-glucose-using activity, so the identification is by chemistry only; the cellulose synthases that are characterised are single-chain GT-2 glycosyltransferases whose additional domains (PilZ/c-di-GMP) are regulatory, so the family is monofunctional.
direction_note: Glycosyl transfer from the sugar nucleotide onto the growing glucan is effectively irreversible in the polymerising direction; ModelSEED's definition ('GDP => GDP-glucose') is a mangled rendering of the KEGG equation GDP + cellulose <=> GDP-glucose + cellulose, so the direction field here is not physically meaningful.

organism_context: Methanocaldococcus (Methanococcus) jannaschii and other methanogens; coenzyme M biosynthesis
rationale: ComA carries a single activity, the stereospecific Michael addition of sulfite to phosphoenolpyruvate; the following steps of coenzyme M biosynthesis are separate proteins (ComB phosphatase, ComC dehydrogenase, ComDE decarboxylase).
direction_note: ComA runs as a synthase (PEP + sulfite -> (2R)-phospho-3-sulfolactate) in coenzyme M biosynthesis; ModelSEED writes the sulfo-lyase direction as forward, i.e. the reverse of the physiological reaction, which supports the LLM's '<'.

enzyme_name: methylsterol monooxygenase (sterol 4alpha-methyl oxidase; ERG25 / MSMO1-SC4MOL / plant SMO1)
organism_context: Fungi (ERG25, two paralogues in Aspergillus fumigatus), mammals (MSMO1/SC4MOL), plants (SMO1/SMO2 families)
rationale: The 4alpha-methyl -> 4alpha-carboxylate conversion is three successive oxidations by one di-iron membrane oxygenase, i.e. one catalytic activity applied iteratively; the subsequent decarboxylation and ketoreduction are carried out by separate proteins (ERG26/NSDHL and ERG27/HSD17B7) in a complex, not by fused domains.
direction_note: The real chemistry is O2- and NADPH-consuming and irreversible toward the carboxylate; the ModelSEED equation has CO2 as a substrate and only one NADPH, so the written stoichiometry does not represent the enzyme's reaction.

organism_context: Arabidopsis thaliana, Chlamydia, cyanobacteria, Leptospira and other prokaryotes using the DapL variant of the DAP/lysine pathway (two diverged forms, DapL1 and DapL2)
rationale: A single PLP-dependent class-I aminotransferase activity that directly transaminates tetrahydrodipicolinate to LL-DAP, replacing the three-enzyme acyl route; no second catalytic activity is reported.
direction_note: Physiologically DapL runs biosynthetically (THDP + L-glutamate -> LL-DAP + 2-oxoglutarate); ModelSEED writes the opposite direction (LL-DAP + 2-oxoglutarate -> THDP + glutamate) as forward, so the LLM's '<' agrees with the pathway direction.

organism_context: Bifunctional as a single fused polypeptide in fungi - CrtYB of Xanthophyllomyces dendrorhous, AL-2 of Neurospora crassa, CarRP of Mucorales. The bacterial (CrtY) and plant (LCYB/CrtL) cyclases are separate, monofunctional proteins.
rationale: KEGG assigns R07856 to KO K06443 (lycopene beta-cyclase); in fungi the cyclase domain is genuinely fused on one chain to a phytoene synthase domain, giving two distinct catalytic activities in one gene product, while the beta-zeacarotene substrate itself is a fungal/plant pathway intermediate.
direction_note: As written the reaction forms a second beta ring (beta-zeacarotene -> 7,8-dihydro-beta-carotene), which is the cyclase's irreversible biosynthetic direction; the systematic name 'beta-end group lyase (decyclizing)' describes the formal reverse and is the likely source of the LLM's '<'.

organism_context: Nicotine degradation (pyridine pathway) in Arthrobacter nicotinovorans and relatives
rationale: KEGG R07947 carries no EC and no KO and is annotated 'spontaneous'; the ring closure/hydration between 2,6-dihydroxy-N-methylmyosmine and 2,6-dihydroxypseudooxynicotine is non-enzymatic, so there is no catalysing protein to classify (the next step, cleavage of 2,6-dihydroxypseudooxynicotine, is a separate hydrolase).
direction_note: Catabolic flux runs through the hydrated, ring-opened form (2,6-dihydroxy-N-methylmyosmine + H2O -> 2,6-dihydroxypseudooxynicotine); ModelSEED writes the dehydration/ring-closure as forward, against the pathway, and in any case the step is a spontaneous equilibrium rather than a directed enzymatic one.

organism_context: Plants making 5-deoxyflavonoids (legumes such as Medicago/Lotus, Acacia and related tannin producers)
rationale: KEGG R08000 has no EC and no KO, so the assignment is inferred from the chemistry: reduction of the dihydroflavonol garbanzol at C-4 to the flavan-3,4-diol 5-deoxyleucopelargonidin is the DFR reaction; DFR is a single-activity NADPH-dependent SDR-family reductase, and its ability to accept flavanones as well as dihydroflavonols is substrate promiscuity within the same reduction chemistry, not a second catalytic activity.
direction_note: DFR runs reductively (garbanzol + NADPH -> 5-deoxyleucopelargonidin) in flavonoid/proanthocyanidin biosynthesis; ModelSEED writes the oxidation as forward and has dropped the NADP+/NADPH pair entirely.

organism_context: Plants making 5-deoxyflavonoids / condensed tannins (e.g. Acacia, Robinia, Medicago)
rationale: KEGG R08001 carries no EC and no KO; by chemistry this is the same DFR step as rxn07790, reducing the dihydroflavonol fustin to the flavan-3,4-diol fisetinidol-3,4-diol (leucofisetinidin). DFR is a single-activity NADPH-dependent SDR reductase.
direction_note: The biosynthetic direction is fustin + NADPH -> leucofisetinidin; ModelSEED writes the oxidation as forward with the nicotinamide cofactor omitted.
